Reasons: the class is UNRESOLVED, so the desk can't tell whether this is operator-backed or a factory coin. The coin is 31 minutes old and 31% off its 30-minute high after a 2x run, and the last 15 minutes show more sellers (618) than net buying (net flow +23.9 SOL on 487 SOL bought, with 463 sold). memos.scout:
The strongest honest case: the coin is alive at 30.9 minutes with a 207% gain over 30 minutes and a 20.6% gain in the last 15 minutes. Last-15-minute activity is substantial: 708 buyers against 618 sellers, $111.7k volume, and net flow still positive at +23.9 SOL, meaning buyers slightly outweighed sellers in the most recent window. Breadth looks organic: 130 early buyers, top-5 buyer share only 26.6%, and no airdrop dump or factory pattern flagged. Pool depth of 155 SOL is decent for a $20 ticket.

The case is weak, though. The coin sits 31% below its 30-minute high, and the early tape was sell-heavy (sell-to-buy ratio 0.84) with a launch bot present. Curve data, graduation timing, and operator structure are all unknown, so we can't tell whether recent buying is durable or a late-stage pump. Sellers were nearly as numerous as buyers, and 463 SOL sold against 487 bought is close to a wash. Given the base rates for buying into alive coins at this age, the evidence supports only a tentative case, not a confident buy.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: a distribution fade after the sharp run. The coin is up 207% over the last 15 minutes (return 0.2057 over the window, return_30_min 2.07), but it has already dropped 31% from its 30-minute high, and sell volume (463 SOL) nearly matches buy volume (487 SOL) with sellers (618) close to buyers (708). Net flow of only +23.9 SOL on $111k of volume means the bid is thin and early holders are exiting into the pump. With a launch bot present, sell-to-buy of 0.84 in the first two minutes, and a pool of only 155 SOL, a 1.4-5.1% round trip cost is significant. Any bounce could be absorbed by sellers, leaving us holding the bag. Skip.
